title:
To make technical corrections to the Water Resources Development Act of 1999.

S
reference: Amends the Water Resources Development Act of 1999 to: (1) authorize appropriations for FY 1999 through 2009 for implementation of a long-term resource monitoring program with respect to the Upper Mississippi River Environmental Management Program (currently, such funding is designated for a program for the planning, construction, and evaluation of measures for fish and wildlife habitat rehabilitation and enhancement); (2) authorize the Secretary of the Army to carry out modifications to the navigation project for the Delaware River, Pennsylvania and Delaware, if such project as modified is technically sound, environmentally (currently, economically) acceptable, and economically justified; (3) subject certain previously deauthorized water resources development projects to the seven-year limitation governing project deauthorizations under the Act, with the exception of such a project for Indian River County, Florida; (4) except from a certain schedule of the non-Federal cost of the periodic nourishment of shore protection projects constructed after December 31, 1999, those projects for which a District Engineer's Report has been completed by such date;  (5) require that the project cooperation agreement for the Comite River Diversion Project for flood control include a provision that specifies that any reduction in the non-Federal share that results from certain modifications be credited toward the share of project costs to be paid by the Amite River Basin Drainage and Water Conservation District; (6) allow the Secretary to provide additional compensation to Chesapeake City, Maryland (currently, to the City of Chesapeake, Maryland) for damage to its water supply resulting from the Chesapeake and Delaware Canal Project; (7) provide for the submission of certain reports on water resources development projects by the Secretary, notwithstanding Federal reporting termination provisions; and (8) authorize and provide for an authorization of appropriations for the existing program for the safety and operations expenses of the Federal Railroad Administration, and make available for obligation funds currently appropriated for such program.
base_model: This bill makes technical corrections to the Water Resources Development Act of 1999. It increases funding for specific water infrastructure projects in Jackson County, Mississippi, Manchester, New Hampshire, Atlanta, Georgia, Paterson, Passaic County, and Passaic Valley, New Jersey, and Elizabeth and North Hudson, New Jersey. The bill also modifies the Upper Mississippi River Environmental Management Program and the Delaware River, Pennsylvania, and Delaware project. Lastly, it reauthorizes several projects and requires the Secretary to determine that each project is technically sound, environmentally acceptable, and economically justified before construction can begin.
finetuned:
This bill makes technical corrections to the Water Resources 
Development Act of 1999. It increases the authorized amount for 
environmental infrastructure projects in Jackson County, Mississippi, 
Manchester, New Hampshire, Atlanta, Georgia, Paterson, Passaic County, 
and Passaic Valley, New Jersey, and Elizabeth and North Hudson, New 
Jersey. It also changes the authorization for the Upper Mississippi River 
Environmental Management Program. The bill also reauthorizes several 
projects.

title:
Federal Forage Fee Act of 1993

That this Act may be cited as the ``Federal Fora
reference:
Federal Forage Fee Act of 1993 - Subjects grazing operations on Federal land to applicable Federal, State, and local environmental and land use requirements. 
Sets forth a forage fee formula for lands under the jurisdiction of the Department of Agriculture and the Department of the Interior.
base_model: The Federal Forage Fee Act of 1993 is a law that aims to charge a reasonable and equitable fee for the use of forage on public lands. This act is in response to the interdependence between public and private lands for forage, water, and wildlife habitat in many western regions. The Act requires all grazing operations on federal lands to comply with various environmental and land use laws, including the Clean Air Act, Endangered Species Act, and National Environmental Policy Act, among others. The Act also emphasizes the importance of cooperative agreements and partnerships in managing and preserving these renewable resources for the benefit of both wildlife and livestock, as well as the rural communities that depend on them.
finetuned:
This bill establishes a forage fee on public lands used for grazing.
The fee is to be based on the fair market value of the forage. The bill
also requires that grazing operations on public lands comply with all
applicable federal, state, and local laws.

title:
Merchant Marine of World War II Congressional Gold Medal Act

SECTION 1. SHORT T
reference: .  Merchant Marine of World War II Congressional Gold Medal Act (Sec. 3) This bill requires the Speaker of the House of Representatives and the President pro tempore of the Senate to arrange for the award, on behalf of Congress, of a single gold medal to the U.S. Merchant Marine of World War II, in recognition of their dedicated and vital service during World War II.  Following its award the medal shall be given to the American Merchant Marine Museum where it will be available for display and research.
base_model: The Merchant Marine of World War II Congressional Gold Medal Act honors the United States Merchant Marine for their crucial role in providing supplies, equipment, and personnel to the armed forces during World War II. This bill recognizes the Merchant Marine's significant contributions to the Allied victory, their higher per capita casualty rate, and their instrumental role in various landing operations, including D-Day. The bill aims to award the Merchant Marine with a Congressional Gold Medal to commemorate their service and sacrifices during the war.
finetuned:
This bill authorizes the President to award a Congressional Gold Medal, 
on behalf of the Congress, to the United States Merchant Marine of World 
War II.

title: To amend the Internal Revenue Code of 1986 to provide for unified income taxatio
reference: Small Business Modernization Act of 2004 - Amends the Internal Revenue Code to: (1) terminate subchapter S corporation elections after 2004 and subchapter S status after 2014 and to allow privately-held domestic corporations, in lieu of electing subchapter S treatment, to elect to be treated as partnerships for tax purposes; (2) set forth rules for the tax treatment of former subchapter S corporations electing partnership status; and (3) exclude from net earnings from self-employment partnership income attributable to capital.
base_model:
The Small Business Tax Modernization Act of 2004 aims to simplify the taxation of pass-through entities, which are businesses that are not taxed as corporations but instead pass their income to their owners.

Key provisions include:
1. No new S corporation elections can be made after December 31, 2004. Existing S corporations will continue to be taxed as such until December 31, 2014, after which they will be treated as partnerships for tax purposes.

2. Certain corporations can elect to be taxed as partnerships for tax purposes, starting from the bill's enactment. This election will not result in any gain or loss recognition for the corporation or its shareholders, except as provided in section 1379A.

This bill affects pass-through entities, particularly S corporations, and changes the way they are taxed under the Internal Revenue Code of 1986.
finetuned:
This bill would amend the Internal Revenue Code of 1986 to provide for 
unified income taxation with respect to pass-through entities.

The bill would terminate the authority to make an S corporation election 
after December 31, 2004.

The bill would allow eligible corporations to elect to be treated as a 
partnership for purposes of the Internal Revenue Code.

The bill would apply to taxable years beginning after December 31, 2004.

title:
Fair Access to Investment Research Act of 2016

SECTION 1. SHORT TITLE.

    Thi
reference: Fair Access to Investment Research Act of 2016 This bill directs the Securities and Exchange Commission (SEC) to revise a specified regulation to create a safe harbor for certain publications or distributions of research reports by brokers or dealers distributing securities. The revised regulation shall declare that a published or distributed investment fund research report shall not be deemed to constitute an offer for sale or an offer to sell a security that is the subject of the offering pursuant to an effective registration statement, even if the broker or dealer is participating or will participate in the registered offering of the covered investment fund's securities. The covered investment fund research report shall indeed be deemed to satisfy the regulation's requirements as well as those of any self-regulatory organization. The SEC shall not impose specified conditions and requirements when implementing the safe harbor.  Until the SEC has adopted such safe harbor revisions, and the Financial Industry Regulatory Authority (FINRA) has revised a related rule, a covered investment fund shall be deemed to be a security listed on a national securities exchange that is not subject to a certain filing requirement of the Investment Company Act of 1940.
base_model: The Fair Access to Investment Research Act of 2016 aims to protect investment fund research reports published or distributed by brokers or dealers. This act expands the safe harbor for such reports, ensuring they are not considered as an offer for sale or an offer to sell a security that is part of a registered offering. The act also stipulates that these reports will be deemed to satisfy certain conditions for the Commission's rules and regulations under the Federal securities laws and the rules of any self-regulatory organization. The Securities and Exchange Commission (SEC) has been instructed to propose and adopt revisions to the safe harbor within specific timeframes, and in doing so, they are prohibited from conditioning the safe harbor on whether the broker or dealer's publication or distribution of a covered investment fund research report constitutes their initiation or reinitiation of research coverage on the covered investment fund or its securities. The act also specifies that the SEC should not require the covered investment fund to have been registered as an investment company or subject to certain reporting requirements for any period exceeding the period of time referenced under the act.
finetuned:
This bill expands the safe harbor for investment fund research reports.

Under current law, a broker or dealer can publish research on a 
registered investment company without the research being considered an 
offer to sell securities. This bill expands that safe harbor to cover 
research on investment funds in continuous distribution.

The bill does not require investment companies to be registered or 
subject to reporting requirements for any period exceeding the period 
of time referenced under the current safe harbor.

title:
Veterans Access to Care Act of 2014

SECTION 1. SHORT TITLE.

    This Act may be
reference: Veterans Access to Care Act of 2014 - Directs the Secretary of Veterans Affairs to enter into agreements with non-VA health care providers to furnish hospital care and medical services to veterans who reside more than 40 miles from a VA medical facility or who have been unable to schedule an appointment within 30 days of the veterans' preferred date or the date determined to be medically necessary. Requires the Secretary to establish a system to track medical appointment wait times. Authorizes the Secretary to enter into agreements with the Department of Defense to share health care resources. Directs the Secretary to improve VA staffing by providing assistance to veterans seeking employment with the VA.
base_model: The Veterans Access to Care Act of 2014 is a comprehensive legislation aimed at improving healthcare access for veterans across the United States. This act addresses long wait times and other barriers that veterans face when seeking medical treatment at VA facilities. The bill proposes several measures to ensure timely access to healthcare for veterans, including the establishment of a system to monitor and track appointment wait times at VA medical centers. The legislation requires the VA to partner with non-VA healthcare providers to offer alternative care options to veterans who live more than 40 miles from a VA facility or who have faced excessive wait times of 30 days or more. The act also emphasizes the need to improve staffing levels at VA medical centers by providing assistance to veterans seeking employment at the VA.
finetuned:
This bill directs the Secretary of Veterans Affairs to enter into 
agreements with non-VA health care providers to provide care to veterans 
who live more than 40 miles from a VA medical facility or who cannot 
get an appointment within 30 days.

The bill also requires the VA to establish a system to track wait 
times and directs the Secretary to improve VA staffing.

title:
Affordable Prescription Drug Act

SECTION 1. SHORT TITLE.

    This Act may be ci
reference: Affordable Prescription Drug Act - Authorizes the Secretary of Health and Human Services to negotiate drug prices under Medicare Part D. Requires the Secretary to negotiate with drug manufacturers to achieve the lowest possible price for covered drugs. Caps Medicare beneficiary out-of-pocket costs for prescription drugs at $2,000 per year. Requires drug manufacturers who increase prices above the rate of inflation to pay a rebate to the federal government. Directs the Secretary to establish a process for importing prescription drugs from Canada.
base_model: The Affordable Prescription Drug Act is a sweeping legislative proposal aimed at reducing the cost of prescription drugs for American consumers, particularly seniors on Medicare. The legislation would give the Department of Health and Human Services the authority to directly negotiate drug prices with pharmaceutical manufacturers for the first time since the creation of Medicare Part D in 2003. The bill targets the most expensive drugs — those without generic competitors — and would use international pricing benchmarks from countries like Canada, Germany, and the United Kingdom as reference points. Critics in the pharmaceutical industry argue the measure would reduce incentives for innovation and research and development of new life-saving drugs, while supporters point to polling showing broad bipartisan support for allowing Medicare to negotiate.
finetuned:
This bill authorizes the Secretary of Health and Human Services to 
negotiate prescription drug prices under Medicare Part D.

The bill caps out-of-pocket drug costs for Medicare beneficiaries at 
$2,000 per year. Drug manufacturers who raise prices faster than the 
rate of inflation must pay rebates to the federal government.

The bill also directs the Secretary to establish a process for 
importing prescription drugs from Canada.

title:
Clean Energy Innovation and Deployment Act

SECTION 1. SHORT TITLE.
reference: Clean Energy Innovation and Deployment Act - Establishes a Clean Energy Deployment Administration within the Department of Energy to provide loan guarantees and grants for the commercial deployment of clean energy technologies. Requires electric utilities to obtain 80 percent of their electricity from clean energy sources by 2035. Creates a Clean Energy Manufacturing Tax Credit for domestic production of renewable energy components. Authorizes $10 billion over five years for energy storage research and deployment. Directs the Administrator of the Environmental Protection Agency to update emissions standards for existing power plants.
base_model: The Clean Energy Innovation and Deployment Act is a landmark piece of legislation that aims to accelerate the United States' transition to a clean energy economy. At its core, the bill establishes a new Clean Energy Deployment Administration within the Department of Energy, charged with providing financial support in the form of loan guarantees and direct grants to companies seeking to commercialize clean energy technologies at scale. The bill sets an ambitious goal requiring all electric utilities to derive at least 80 percent of their electricity from clean sources by 2035. This would include solar, wind, nuclear, geothermal, and hydroelectric power. Additionally, the legislation creates a new manufacturing tax credit designed to incentivize domestic production of solar panels, wind turbines, and battery storage systems, with the goal of creating American jobs and reducing dependence on foreign supply chains for critical clean energy components.
finetuned:
This bill establishes a Clean Energy Deployment Administration within 
the Department of Energy to provide loan guarantees and grants for 
clean energy technologies.

The bill requires electric utilities to obtain 80 percent of their 
electricity from clean energy sources by 2035 and creates a tax credit 
for domestic clean energy manufacturing.

The bill also authorizes $10 billion for energy storage research and 
directs the EPA to update power plant emissions standards.

title:
American Data Privacy Protection Act

SECTION 1. SHORT TITLE.
reference: American Data Privacy Protection Act - Establishes requirements for data collection and processing by covered entities. Requires covered entities to provide clear notice of data practices and obtain opt-in consent before processing sensitive personal data. Grants individuals the right to access, correct, and delete their personal data. Prohibits the sale of precise geolocation data and health data without explicit consent. Grants the Federal Trade Commission civil penalty authority of up to $50,000 per day per violation. Preempts inconsistent State privacy laws.
base_model: The American Data Privacy Protection Act represents a landmark attempt by Congress to establish a unified federal standard for data privacy in the United States, where currently a patchwork of state laws governs how companies collect and use personal data. The legislation would apply to any company that collects data on more than 100,000 individuals annually and would require these companies to clearly disclose what data they collect, how it is used, and with whom it is shared. The bill gives American consumers meaningful new rights over their personal information, including the right to access the data companies have collected about them, the right to request corrections, and the right to have that data deleted. Companies that violate the Act's requirements would face civil penalties of up to $50,000 per day per violation, enforceable by the Federal Trade Commission.
finetuned:
This bill establishes federal data privacy requirements for companies 
that collect personal data.

Covered companies must provide clear notice of data practices and obtain 
consent before sharing sensitive data. Individuals have the right to 
access, correct, and delete their personal data.

The Federal Trade Commission is authorized to impose civil penalties of 
up to $50,000 per day per violation. The bill preempts inconsistent 
state privacy laws.

title:
Second Chance Reauthorization Act of 2015

SECTION 1. SHORT TITLE.
reference: Second Chance Reauthorization Act of 2015 - Reauthorizes and amends the Second Chance Act of 2007. Directs the Attorney General to make grants to states, local governments, and nonprofit organizations to provide reentry services for individuals released from prisons and jails. Authorizes grants for mentoring, job training, substance abuse treatment, and housing assistance. Requires grantees to collect data on recidivism rates and employment outcomes. Establishes a Federal Reentry Council to coordinate reentry policy across federal agencies. Authorizes $415 million over five years.
base_model: The Second Chance Reauthorization Act of 2015 extends and strengthens the landmark Second Chance Act of 2007, which first created a federal framework for supporting individuals returning to their communities after incarceration. The legislation recognizes that the United States has the world's highest incarceration rate and that the vast majority of incarcerated individuals will eventually be released, making successful reintegration a matter of vital public safety interest. The bill directs the Attorney General to administer competitive grants to state and local governments, as well as nonprofit organizations, for a wide array of reentry services. These include transitional housing, job training and placement, substance abuse and mental health treatment, and mentoring programs. Grantees are required to collect longitudinal data on outcomes including recidivism rates and employment, enabling rigorous evaluation of program effectiveness.
finetuned:
This bill reauthorizes the Second Chance Act of 2007, which provides 
grants for prisoner reentry programs.

The bill directs the Attorney General to award grants to states, local 
governments, and nonprofits for reentry services including job training, 
substance abuse treatment, mentoring, and housing assistance.

Grantees must track recidivism and employment outcomes. The bill 
authorizes $415 million over five years and establishes a Federal 
Reentry Council to coordinate policy across agencies.
